text: The dataset preparation pipeline begins with gathering the required data sources.
These inputs include recordings across six crowd video experiments, pedestrian trajectory data, and corresponding ground truth annotations.
In the local region extraction phase, candidate spatial patches associated with individuals are extracted from the video frames.
A duplicate removal step then filters out redundant and overlapping extracted regions.
This produces a clean set of local image regions representing individuals and their local neighborhoods.
Next, during local region labeling, samples are annotated, with red borders denoting pushing behaviors and green borders indicating non-pushing behaviors.
Finally, the annotated patches are partitioned into dedicated training, validation, and testing subsets across the experimental video sources.
